title: Sachems Who Played in College & Beyond
status: Research in progress; additions require verified college or professional football roster evidence. Saugus, Massachusetts, not Saugus, California.
eligibility: A documented college or professional roster spot qualifies even without game appearances; redshirts, reserves, and practice squads count. Being drafted or invited to a tryout does not alone establish a professional roster spot.

entries.name: Steve Gannon
entries.professional: Cincinnati Bengals (signed and released in 1980); New York Giants (claimed on waivers and released in 1980)
entries.notes: All-New England defensive end at Holy Cross; 1975 Lynn Item All-Star at Saugus. In 1980 he signed as an NFL free agent with Cincinnati, was released, joined the New York Giants on waivers, and was subsequently released during preseason roster cuts. Contemporary newspaper clippings document both NFL transactions. Holy Cross Hall of Fame inductee (2020).

entries.name: John Nicolo
entries.notes: Four-year football and baseball letterwinner at Ithaca College. An All-American running back on Ithaca's 1979 NCAA Division III national championship football team, he also captained the 1980 NCAA Division III national championship baseball team as its shortstop. Named 1980 Division III College World Series Most Valuable Player after setting tournament records with 12 hits and nine runs. Both Ithaca championship teams have been inducted into the college's Athletic Hall of Fame (1979 football in 2014; 1980 baseball in 2019). After college, played one professional minor-league baseball season for the Auburn Americans in 1980 (42 games, 40 hits in 154 at-bats, .260 batting average, 25 runs).

entries.name: Raphael Zammit
entries.notes: Curry running back, 2000–2003. Career: 800 carries, 4,353 rushing yards, 44 rushing TDs; 46 kickoff returns for 1,131 yards and 2 punt-return TDs. 2002: 1,479 rushing yards, 18 rushing TDs; 2003: 1,587 rushing yards, 12 rushing TDs. First Team All-Conference (2002, 2003); Second Team All-Conference (2000, 2001); Conference Offensive Player of the Year (2002, 2003); National Third Team All-American (2002, 2003); ECAC All-Region First Team (2002, 2003); NEFWA Division II/III All-Star (2002, 2003); NEFWA Gold Helmet weekly award (2002, 2003). Source: Curry College Football Record Book, updated January 2025.

entries.notes: Member of Plymouth State's football roster from 1988 through 1991. Listed at running back. Saugus's 1987 captain directory identifies Barressi as a senior captain; class of 1988 corroborated by his 1988 freshman college roster.

entries.name: Joe Attubato
entries.notes: Listed on Plymouth State's 1994–1997 football rosters; defensive lineman and 1997 team captain. Saugus's 1993 captain directory and a 1994 Lynn Item season preview identify him as a graduating Saugus player headed to Plymouth State.

entries.name: Colt Meredith
entries.notes: Saugus High School Class of 1996; Plymouth State College Class of 2000. Played linebacker and defensive back for Plymouth State from 1996 through 1999, serving as a team captain in 1999. Named the 1999 Freedom Football Conference Defensive Player of the Year and earned Hewlett-Packard/SID Division III All-America Honorable Mention as a defensive back. The honors are corroborated by Plymouth State's official records and a 2007 Lynn Daily Item obituary.
